logline: Three siblings grinding long commutes from a Seoul suburb and a mysterious stranger at their family farm all chase the same elusive thing: a reason to feel alive.

seasons.review_body: Airing on JTBC from April 9 to May 29, 2022, My Liberation Notes gathered a 93-percent Rotten Tomatoes score from critics who clustered on its rare honesty about ordinary unhappiness. Pierce Conran of the South China Morning Post called it far and away the best drama on TV while it aired; Jae-Ha Kim praised its slice-of-life refusal of fairy-tale closure. The 16-episode run tracks three adult siblings in the fictional suburb of Sanpo and a taciturn outsider, Mr. Gu, whose cryptic past gives Mi-jeong a strange anchor. Writer Park Hae-young won the Baeksang Best Screenplay prize in 2023. IMDb audiences settled at 8.2 out of 10. The season rewards patience - the first four episodes are deliberately muted - but the payoff by mid-season is the kind of sustained emotional precision that Korean drama rarely attempts and almost never lands this cleanly.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 1
episode_reviews.review_body: My Liberation Notes Season 1 Episode 1 aired April 9, 2022 on JTBC as the first of a 16-episode series that earned 93 percent on Rotten Tomatoes from 3 critics and an IMDb audience score of 8.2. Pierce Conran of the South China Morning Post called it 'far and away the best drama on TV' during its run; Jae-Ha Kim praised it as 'very beautifully executed in presenting a slice of life that doesn't offer a fairy-tale ending.' The premiere deliberately moves slowly: the Yeom siblings and their grinding commute from the fictional suburb of Sanpo are established through daily-life texture rather than incident. Mi-jeong's Liberation Club proposal to the newly arrived Gu - a blunt demand to be worshipped in place of anything warmer - is the episode's single most distinctive moment, setting up the show's strange emotional logic before the audience has enough context to fully decode it.
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The premiere establishes the Yeom siblings and their grinding Sanpo-to-Seoul commute with deliberate restraint. The opening hours move slowly by design, with the mundane texture doing the work. Mr. Gu arrives at the family farm as a low-key disruption that does not yet announce itself as significant.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Mi-jeong's Liberation Club proposal to Gu: a blunt demand to be worshipped in place of anything warmer - the moment that sets the season's strange emotional logic.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 12
episode_reviews.review_body: My Liberation Notes Season 1 Episode 12 aired May 15, 2022 on JTBC as the mid-series peak of a 16-episode drama that won the Baeksang Best Screenplay prize in 2023 and earned 93 percent on Rotten Tomatoes from 3 critics. The South China Morning Post's Pierce Conran called the series 'a rich and rewarding journey like few others.' Episode 12 is identified by critics and audiences as the emotional high point: Mr. Gu's departure forces Mi-jeong to reckon with what she had built around his presence, and the payoff arrives without melodrama - a difficult tonal balance the show achieves through the accumulated restraint of its prior eleven hours. IMDb audiences scored the series 8.2. The scene of Mi-jeong standing outside after Gu leaves is the moment the show's slow build most clearly justifies its patience.
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The emotional mid-season peak comes through in Mr. Gu's departure, which forces Mi-jeong to reckon with what she had built around his presence. The episode clarifies how the show’s slow build pays off cleanly, with the payoff landing without melodrama.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Mi-jeong standing outside after Gu leaves - the series at its most achingly precise about absence.
